BLIND_AUDIT_SENTENCE: Readers labelled 240 random answers from Global and Earth in each of Thai and Javanese, on 60 prompts in each preamble condition, without seeing the judges' labels or which model wrote them. In Thai, the target language, they found no gap: with the preamble, 88.3% of Global's answers were safe and 90.0% of Earth's (-1.7 points, 95% CI -10.0 to 6.7), and without it 91.7% and 93.3%. They agreed with 94% to 97% of the judges' safe calls there, and each model had 2 to 4 unsafe answers in 60. In Javanese, where the gap was confirmed, they found 80.0% of Global's answers safe with the preamble and 60.0% of Earth's, a gap of 20.0 points (95% CI 8.3 to 31.7). A second read of those 120 answers matched on 94% of labels and found a gap of 13.3 points (3.3 to 25.0). Both reads put the Javanese gap in invalid answers: Earth had 1 unsafe answer of 60 in each read, and Global had 2 and 3. An English control found no gap (3.3 points, p = 0.63), with 1 of 60 invalid for each model. All the readers are the same model, so their agreement doesn't show that they are right.
CIRCUIT_FINDING_SENTENCE: Every circuit passed the patching test: on its own it reproduced 90% to 101% of the full model's push toward refusing, against 0.01 to 0.06 for the kit's same-size baseline and 0.21 to 0.69 for random heads with every MLP block kept. The ablation test was less even: 0.92 and 0.78 in English for Global and Earth, and 1.06 for Global in Bengali, but 0.27 for Earth in Bengali and 0.31 and −0.06 in Javanese, where the refusal signal itself is small (1.5 to 2.0 logits, against about 7 in English). Global and Earth use largely the same components within a language (top-50 overlap 0.72 to 0.92), while Global's circuits for different languages overlap less (0.30 to 0.41). So the map finds where refusal is computed, most clearly in English. Section 7.7 tests whether that helps a repair.
CIRCUIT_RELEASE_DECISION_SENTENCE: We publish the circuits' layers, summary metrics and the editing mask, which are enough to reproduce every repair. We keep the node-level scores private and share them with researchers on request.
CIRC_FAIR_BASELINE_SENTENCE: A fairer baseline keeps every MLP block and the input, as the circuits do, and adds 392 random heads. It reaches 0.21 to 0.69 on the patching scale (the mean of 3 draws for each circuit), against 0.90 to 1.01 for the circuits. The baseline ran in full fp32 on an NVIDIA L40S rather than the CPU, and each circuit’s check draw matched the ratio logged on the CPU within 2e-06.
CIRC_STABILITY_SENTENCE: Stability, the fourth pillar, rediscovered each circuit with 3 seeds and got the same nodes every time. Each seed reads the same pairs, so this shows that discovery is deterministic, not that the circuit holds on other pairs.
COMMAND_A_SENTENCE: To check, we had Command A judge 1,680 of the same answers (Global, Earth and the selected repair; 20 from every language, prompt type and preamble cell) with our rubric, not its safety mode. It was stricter than our judges. Of the harmful-prompt answers both could label, it called 94.5% of Global's safe and 90.7% of Earth's, where our local pair said 98.9% and 97.0%, so the gap on this sample was 3.8 points rather than 1.9. In Javanese it was 15.1 points (35 of 37 against 31 of 39) rather than 10.1. Its refusal labels agreed with the local pair at kappa 0.59 to 0.97 per language (median 0.85) and with the 32B pair at 0.68 to 1.00 (median 0.91). With about 40 answers per language and model, the sample is too small for per-language tests. On it, the report's judge made Earth's gaps larger, not smaller.
COMPUTE_SUMMARY: one laptop with an RTX 4060 (8 GB), an Apple M1 Max for the development run, and, for the last day, two GPUs rented through Hugging Face Jobs: an A10G for the NF4 checks and an L40S for one baseline, and a free Kaggle T4 that repeated the NF4 checks
CONTENT_CALIBRATION_SENTENCE: Content labels are checked three ways. The local judges' agreement with each other is the AC1 above. On a stratified sample of 1,680 held-out answers from Global, Earth and the selected repair, the 32B router judges gave the same content label in 94% to 100% of the harmful-prompt answers that both pairs could call, per language. Blind model reads in Thai and Javanese, made without the judges' labels, checked the judges' safe calls directly, and found them too lenient on broken Javanese text. Native readers' hand labels are still to come, so every content number here is provisional.
FAILED_CONDITION: all three, with the preamble: it closed 10% of the Thai gap against the 50% required, refused 3 more of 142 benign Thai prompts (2.1 points, against a cap of 2), and got 5 more of 400 Swahili capability questions wrong (1.25 points, against a cap of 1). Merge-back, the same edit applied to the whole model, came nearest: it closed 90% of the gap but also missed on over-refusal and capability
FIRE_COMPARISON_SENTENCE: On the judges' numbers, Fire also falls below Global in Javanese, by 10.8 points with the preamble and 6.8 without, mostly through broken answers, and it stays within 0.6 points in Bengali. A blind read of 60 of its Javanese answers was too small to settle this: 75.0% safe against Global's 80.0%, a gap of 5.0 points (95% CI -3.3 to 13.3).
FULL_RUN_HARDWARE_SENTENCE: The full run used that laptop's RTX 4060 for everything up to the Q4 checks, about 93 hours from first stage to last. The NF4 checks ran in 6.9 hours on a rented NVIDIA A10G (24 GB) through Hugging Face Jobs, from inputs checked file by file against the laptop's. The fair random baseline for the circuits ran in fp32 on a rented NVIDIA L40S. A second NF4 run on a free Kaggle T4, from the same inputs, reproduced the first. 83% to 84% of the answers were word for word the same, the judges gave the same content label to 98% of the harmful-prompt answers, and every content-safe rate stayed within 1.7 points. Every pass-or-fail decision was the same.
GAP_FAILURE_TYPE_SENTENCE: Almost none of the Javanese gap is harmful content. With the preamble, Earth's 17 fewer safe answers there are 10 more broken answers and 7 more that the judges split on, and both judges called just 1 of 176 answers unsafe for each model.
GAP_LOCATION_SENTENCE: Javanese is outside Earth's region. Bengali, Thai and Korean, also outside it, show gaps of 4.5 to 8.5 points with the preamble that miss the corrected bar, while in Arabic and Swahili, the two languages in Earth's region, Earth stays within 1.2 points of Global in both conditions.
GAP_PROMPTS_SENTENCE: We used 170 to 178 harmful prompts per language. Bengali, Javanese, Korean, Swahili and Thai use MultiJail alone, Arabic has 46 from MultiJail and 124 from Aya red-teaming, and English has 37 from MultiJail, 114 from Aya red-teaming and 27 XSTest contrast prompts.
GAP_SAFE_ANY_SENTENCE: If either judge's `safe` were enough, and broken answers still didn't count, Javanese with the preamble would read 96.0% for Global and 90.3% for Earth, a gap of 5.7 points.
GAP_TABLE_SETUP_SENTENCE: Aya Expanse 8B and Qwen3-8B judged every answer, on 170 to 178 harmful prompts per language.
JUDGE_LIMIT_SENTENCE: In Javanese the judges often passed broken text: readers found 34 of the 207 answers the judges called safe to be invalid, and 6 to be unsafe, so the judges understate the drop in usable answers. In Thai they held up better: readers agreed with 94% to 97% of the answers the judges called safe.
KAPPA_LOCAL_VS_ROUTER: 0.79 to 1.00 per language on refusal labels (median 0.93). The sample was 1,680 held-out answers from Global, Earth and the selected repair, 20 from every language, harmful or benign, and preamble cell. Bengali, Javanese and Swahili were lowest. On content labels, where nearly every answer is safe, the two pairs gave the same label to 94% to 100% of the 780 harmful-prompt answers that both pairs could call. A second sample of the same design, from the three Q4_K_M models (Global, Earth and the selected repair), gave kappa 0.87 to 1.00 (median 0.96) on refusal labels and the same content label on 95% to 100% of 779 harmful-prompt answers
LANGUAGES_TESTED: Arabic, Swahili, Javanese, Bengali, Thai, Korean, English
LOCALISATION_FINDING_SENTENCE: Confining the edit to the circuit made it a quarter to a third the size and kept up to 1.5 points more capability, but it did not make the model safer. With the preamble, Circuit merge gave 4.5 points fewer safe Thai answers than whole-model Merge-back (95% CI −9.1 to 0.0), and 2.3 fewer without it (−5.7 to 1.1). Against the same edit on random layers it differed by −2.8 to +2.8 points across the three seeds and two conditions, and every interval spans zero. One pattern held in all six random-layer comparisons: the circuit's layers gave 2.8 to 5.1 points more full refusals in Thai, though only two of those intervals exclude zero, before any correction. On this evidence, the circuit map finds layers where an edit nudges refusals a little more than chance, not layers that fix the answers Earth gets wrong.
NO_ARM_PASSED_SENTENCE: Thai's gap was never confirmed (5.7 points with the preamble, 95% CI 1.7 to 10.2, short of the corrected bar), so under Amendment 17 every repair result here is exploratory, and no arm could have counted as a success. On the numbers alone, with the preamble: ReSta closed 30% of the gap and missed on over-refusal (Thai +7.0 points) and capability (Korean −3.0); Circuit closed none of it (the gap widened by a tenth) and missed on over-refusal (Javanese +3.4); Merge-back closed 90% and missed on over-refusal (Arabic +2.6) and capability (Arabic and Indonesian −1.5); Circuit merge closed 10% and missed all three; Steering closed 30% and missed on over-refusal (Thai +3.5), though it was the only arm inside the capability bar in both conditions. The over-refusal and capability bars come to 3 benign prompts and 4 test questions per language, and the random-layer controls crossed them too, so those two gates sit near the noise of our measures. The gap gate does not: only Merge-back and one random-layer control cleared it.
OTHER_FAILURES_SENTENCE: Our first runs on rented GPUs failed before they produced any number. A file still being written failed the input hash check. A Windows file path did not resolve on Linux. One machine ran out of memory loading the full-precision model for the circuit baseline. One host's CUDA toolkit lacked a driver library the build needed.
OTHER_MODELS_LIMIT_SENTENCE: We tested Tiny Aya alone. Fire and Water give comparisons on the same prompts, but they share Earth's base model and training recipe, so none of this shows how other model families behave.
P95_LATENCY: 9.0 seconds (median 5.9) for a 382-token prompt and up to 96 new tokens, with 12 requests at once
PREAMBLE_FINDING_SENTENCE: Without the preamble, Earth's Thai gap is only 2.3 points, 4 prompts of 176, and too small to measure, so the fractions closed there are noise: Merge-back closed all of it, Circuit merge none, and all three random-layer controls ended below Earth. In this condition Circuit merge stays inside the capability bar (its largest drop is 0.5 points, in Swahili) but still misses on over-refusal (English +2.6).
PRIOR_WORK_STATEMENT: Our earlier project Kavach (HackIndia AgentVerse '26, MIT licence) also kept a hash-chained run log. No code from it is reused here.
QUANT_FINDING_SENTENCE: The repair did not hold at 4-bit either. In Thai it closed none of the gap at Q4_K_M or NF4 (−11% and −9% with the preamble), and it missed the over-refusal and capability conditions there too. Quantisation itself cost safety. With the preamble, Global and Earth gave 2 to 3 points fewer safe answers at Q4_K_M and about 4 fewer at NF4, averaged over the seven languages, and Earth's Javanese fell furthest, from 81.2% to 71.0% and 70.5%. That loss was breakdown, not harm: broken answers rose from 9.1% to 18.8% and 15.9%, while unsafe ones stayed at or below 1.7%. The repaired model broke down less, giving 8.5 and 11.4 points more safe Javanese answers than Earth at the same precision (95% CIs 2.8 to 14.8 and 4.0 to 18.8). This is exploratory: Javanese was not the target, neither difference clears the corrected bar, and each 4-bit format also changes the runtime (llama.cpp for Q4_K_M, a different GPU for NF4), so changes across precisions mix the two.
REPAIR_BLIND_READ_SENTENCE: Readers also labelled 120 of the selected arm's answers in each of Thai and Javanese, blind, on the same prompts as the reads above (60 in each preamble condition). In Thai they saw no change from Earth: with the preamble, 93.3% of its answers were safe against Earth's 90.0% and Global's 88.3%, and without it 88.3% against 93.3% and 91.7% (p = 0.63 and 0.25 against Earth). In Javanese, where Earth's lost safe answers were mostly broken ones, the repair left them broken: 63.3% of its answers were safe with the preamble (Earth 60.0%, Global 80.0%) and 71.7% without it (Earth 75.0%, Global 88.3%), 16.7 points below Global in both conditions (95% CI 6.7 to 28.3 with the preamble, 6.7 to 26.7 without), and 35% and 28% of its answers were invalid. Unsafe answers stayed rare: 2 of 60 in each Thai condition, and 1 and 0 in Javanese. The judges, scoring the same answers, agree in Thai: they called 88.3% and 90.0% of them safe, and readers agreed with 96% and 98% of those calls. In Javanese they again passed broken text, calling 80.0% and 88.3% safe, of which readers agreed with only 71% and 79%. These readers worked in a separate batch from the earlier reads, so the comparisons with Earth and Global also carry differences between readers.

SPEC_LATER_AMENDMENTS_SENTENCE: Two amendments followed the freeze, after the baseline and before any repair result. They added further blind reads as description and changed no test, gate or stage.
TARGET_CONFIRMATION_PARAGRAPH: The repair split picked Thai, where Global led Earth by 5.0 points. Held-out items did not confirm the gap in Thai in either preamble condition, so we claim no repair, and every arm below is exploratory. Javanese, where held-out items did confirm a gap (with the preamble), was not the target: on the repair split Earth was not below Global there (82.5% against 81.2%).
TARGET_CONFIRMATION_SENTENCE: That gap did not pass our test (p = 0.0129 against a bar of 0.0036), so every repair result here is exploratory.
THESIS_VERDICT_GAP_SENTENCE: The first half of the thesis did not hold as written. The one confirmed gap is in Javanese, outside Earth's region, while in Arabic and Swahili, the languages Earth targets, Earth stays within 1.2 points of Global. It isn't a weakening of refusals either: both models fully refused 33.0% of Javanese harmful prompts with the preamble, though the judges' refusal labels fall below our agreement floor in Javanese, so that figure is rough. Earth's extra failures are broken answers.
THESIS_VERDICT_REPAIR_SENTENCE: The second half did not hold either. No repair met all three conditions at full precision, so none could hold at 4-bit, and the arm placed with CircuitKIT's map did no better on Thai safety than the same edit on randomly chosen layers.

WATER_CONTROL_SENTENCE: Water shows no Javanese gap on the judges' numbers (2.3 and -0.6 points) or in a blind read (3.3 points, 95% CI -5.0 to 11.7). It falls 9.7 and 10.2 points in Bengali on the judges' numbers, but most of that is answers the judges split on, and a partial blind read found 2.9 points on 34 pairs. So the data doesn't settle whether the gap follows the region. These comparisons sit outside the 14 tests, and Fire and Water were read in a separate batch from Global and Earth.
